title: Weighing of the own mark and of the bond against the grip, oscillator cells

key_results.statement: For every grip, the source term $g_sq_{x_s}$ is removed by the unitary shift $q\to q+\phi$, $\phi(x)=-g_sG(x-x_s)$: it enters the eigenvalues only through the shifted grips $F_i(q_{x_i}+\phi(x_i))$ and the body-independent constant $-\tfrac12g_s^2G(0)$ (uncompressed contract, $M\to\infty$ first).

At first order in $g_s$, every weight is $\partial_cX[F_c]\,\Delta\phi$ for $X\in\{\text{cost},C^{(1)},C^{\rm mark}\}$, and $\rho_{\rm mark}=\partial_c\ln C^{\rm mark}/\partial_c\ln C^{(1)}$, independent of the places and of the distance to the source; cost, $C^{(1)}=\mu\langle F\rangle_0$ and $C^{\rm mark}$ are fixed by the total contracts with and without the body.

Field constants $G$, $w_0$, $g_r(\nu)$, $c_r(\tau)$ and $J_n(\mathbf r)=\int_0^\infty c_r^n d\tau$, with $J_1=G/2$, $0<c_r\le c_0\le w_0$, $J_n(\mathbf r)\le w_0^{n-1}J_1(\mathbf r)$, $J_2\le w_0G_0/2$.

Made field ($L\to\infty$ first): in the scaling regime $\ell=\sqrt{\kappa_h}/m_h\gg1$ and $1\ll\lvert d\rvert\ll\ell^3$, $G$ is linear, logarithmic ($K_0$) or $1/(4\pi\kappa_h\lvert d\rvert)$ for $D=1,2,3$ below $\ell$ and decays as $e^{-\lvert d\rvert/\ell}$ above it (chain form exact at every $\ell$); at any $\ell$ and $\lvert d\rvert\gg\max(1,\ell)$, $G\asymp\lvert d\rvert^{-(D-1)/2}e^{-\alpha(\hat d)\lvert d\rvert}$ with the direction-dependent lattice rate $\alpha(\hat n)=\ell^{-1}+O(\ell^{-3})$.
For (G2), a lowest eigenvector exists in the limit $M\to\infty$ iff $1+2\sigma M_kF_2G_0>0$; otherwise the lowest eigenvalue of $C_M$ tends to $-\infty$.

For (G2), exactly: cost $=\mu F_0-\mu^2F_1^2G_0/(2D_\mu)+Z(2\mu F_2)$, $C^{(1)}=\mu(F_0+F_2w_0)$, $C^{\rm mark}=-\mu^2G_0(F_1^2+\zeta)/(2D_\mu)<0$, with $D_\mu=1+2\mu F_2G_0$ and $Z(a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\ln(1+ag(\nu))d\nu$.

Zero-point part of the (G2) mark: $\zeta=\frac{4F_2^2}{\pi G_0}\int_0^\infty g^2(1+2\mu F_2G_0)\chi(2\mu F_2g)d\nu\ge0$, $\zeta=(4F_2^2J_2/G_0)[1+O(\mu F_2G_0)]$, strictly increasing in $\sigma M_kF_2$ for $F_2\ne0$.

For (G2), exactly at first order in $g_s$: $\Delta W=\mu F_1\Delta\phi/D_\mu$, $\Delta W^{(1)}=\mu F_1\Delta\phi$, $\Delta W^{\rm mark}=-2\mu^2F_1F_2G_0\Delta\phi/D_\mu$; the zero-point part is not weighed.

For (G) (classes (Gθ) $F(0)+\theta f$ and (GΦ) $F(0)\Phi(\beta q)$ of note (a)): $C^{(1)}=\mu a_0$ exactly and $C^{\rm mark}=-\mu^2S$, $S=\sum_{n\ge1}a_n^2J_n/n!>0$, $a_n=\langle F^{(n)}(q_x)\rangle_0$, up to $O(\theta^3)$ resp. $O(\beta^4)$; the $a_n$ exist and the series converge; at fixed $g_s$ the Taylor coefficients of the compressed eigenvalue through order $\theta^2$ resp. $\beta^3$ converge to these values as $M\to\infty$ (higher ones not claimed); where $C$ has no lowest eigenvalue the remainder orders are formal.

For (G): $\Delta W^{(1)}=\mu a_1\Delta\phi$ exactly and $\Delta W^{\rm mark}=-2\mu^2T\Delta\phi$, $T=\sum_{n\ge1}a_na_{n+1}J_n/n!$, up to $O(\theta^3)$ for (Gθ) and $O(\beta^5)$ (relative $O(\beta^2)$, level dependent) for (GΦ); formal orders where $C$ has no lowest eigenvalue.

For (GΦ), with $\varepsilon^2=\beta^2w_0$: $a_n=F(0)\beta^n[\Phi^{(n)}(0)+O(\varepsilon^2)]$, $S(\mathbf r)=F(0)^2\beta^2J_1(\mathbf r)[\Phi'(0)^2+O(\varepsilon^2)]$, $T(\mathbf r)=F(0)^2\beta^3J_1(\mathbf r)[\Phi'(0)\Phi''(0)+O(\varepsilon^2)]$, uniformly in $\mathbf r$, and the same for the two-grip sums.

The mark weight vanishes at the lowest order for (Gθ) with $T_f=0$ (e.g. odd $f$) and for (GΦ) with $\Phi''(0)=0$; a nonzero weight can first appear at order $\theta^3$ resp. $\beta^5$ (value not computed), so $\rho_{\rm mark}=O(1)$ (Gθ, $F(0)\ne0$) resp. $O(\beta^2)$.

Bond profile at order $\mu_1\mu_2$ for two grips of the class: $U(\mathbf r)=-2\mu_1\mu_2S_{12}(\mathbf r)$, $S_{12}=\sum_{n\ge1}a_n^{(1)}a_n^{(2)}J_n(\mathbf r)/n!$; for (G2) $U=-\mu_1\mu_2[F_1^{(1)}F_1^{(2)}G(\mathbf r)+4F_2^{(1)}F_2^{(2)}J_2(\mathbf r)]$; for a common grip $U$ has the sign of $-\mu_1\mu_2$, for different grips it can vanish.

Bond weight: $\Delta W_{\rm bond}=-2\mu_1\mu_2[T_{12}(\mathbf r)\Delta\phi_1+T_{21}(\mathbf r)\Delta\phi_2]$, with $\Delta\phi_1+\Delta\phi_2=2m_{\mathbf r}\Delta\bar\phi$; for $d\gg\lvert\mathbf r\rvert$ the midpoint factor is $1+O(\lvert\mathbf r\rvert^2/d^2)$ for $1\ll d\ll\ell$ and $\cosh(t^*\cdot\mathbf r/2)[1+O(\lvert\mathbf r\rvert/d+\lvert t^*\rvert\lvert\mathbf r\rvert^2/d)]$ for $d\gg\max(1,\ell)$, with the lattice decay vector $t^*(\hat d)$ (exactly $\cosh(\alpha r/2)$ for $D=1$); in the scaling regime $\cosh((\mathbf r\cdot\hat d)/(2\ell))[1+O(\lvert\mathbf r\rvert/d+\lvert\mathbf r\rvert^2/(d\ell)+\lvert\mathbf r\rvert/\ell^3)]$; reference to a body gives an error of first order in $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert/\min(d,\ell)$.

For (G2), exactly, two grips: $U=U_{\rm cl}+Z_b$ with $U_{\rm cl}=-\tfrac12v^T\mathbb Mv$, and $\Delta W_{\rm bond}=-2\sum_i\eta_i\Delta\phi_iv_i(\mathbb Mv)_i$, $\eta_i=F_2^{(i)}/F_1^{(i)}$; the zero-point bond $Z_b$ is not weighed; for a common grip $U_{\rm cl}$ and $Z_b$ both have the sign of $-\mu_1\mu_2$.

At order $\mu^2$, for every pair of grips: $\rho_{{\rm mark},i}=2a_0^{(i)}T_i/(a_1^{(i)}S_i)$, $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=(a_0^{(i)}/a_1^{(i)})(T_{12}\Delta\phi_1+T_{21}\Delta\phi_2)/(S_{12}\Delta\bar\phi)$ (single-body midpoint reference of body $i$); common grip: $\rho_{\rm bond}=m_{\mathbf r}\rho(\mathbf r)$, $\rho(\mathbf r)=2a_0T(\mathbf r)/(a_1S(\mathbf r))$; level and branch independent; $\rho_{\rm bond}$ depends on the source distance through $\Delta\phi_j/\Delta\bar\phi$; excluded: $a_0^{(i)}=0$, $a_1^{(i)}=0$, $\Delta\bar\phi=0$, $U=0$.
For (G2), exactly: $\rho_{\rm mark}=4F_2\langle F\rangle_0/(F_1^2+\zeta(\sigma M_kF_2))$.

For (GΦ) at order $\mu^2$, uniformly in $\mathbf r$: $\rho_{{\rm mark},i}=2\Phi_i''(0)/\Phi_i'(0)^2+O(\varepsilon^2)$ and $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=(\kappa_1\Delta\phi_1+\kappa_2\Delta\phi_2)/(\Phi_i'(0)\Delta\bar\phi)+O(\varepsilon^2)$, $\kappa_j=\Phi_j''(0)/\Phi_j'(0)$; higher orders add relative $O(\beta^2)$.

At leading order in $\beta$, $\rho_{{\rm mark},i}=1$ and $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=m_{\mathbf r}$ for both bodies, every level and both branches, at every distance and separation, on all three graphs and all $L,\kappa_h,m_h>0$ with $\varepsilon,u\ll1$, iff both grips are square, $2F(0)F''(0)=F'(0)^2$ (in (G2) $4F_0F_2=F_1^2$), with a common $\hat\beta=F'(0)/(2F(0))$; $m_{\mathbf r}=1+O(\lvert\mathbf r\rvert^2/\min(d,\ell)^2)$ for $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert\ll\min(d,\ell)$.

Common square (G2) grip at order $\mu^2$: $\rho(\mathbf r)=(1+\beta^2w_0)/(1+\beta^2J_2(\mathbf r)/G(\mathbf r))$, so $\rho_{\rm mark}-1=\beta^2(w_0-J_2/G_0)\in[\beta^2w_0/2,\beta^2w_0)$ and $\rho_{\rm bond}/m_{\mathbf r}-1\to\beta^2w_0$ for $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert\gg\ell$, up to $O(\varepsilon^4)$, both independent of the source distance; level dependence at relative order $\varepsilon^2u$.

In the (G2) eigenvector with one quantum in the uniform mode the weights are unchanged, $\rho_{\rm mark}=4F_2(\langle F\rangle_0+F_2/(N_fm_h))/(F_1^2+\zeta_1)$ with $\zeta_1-\zeta=O(F_2^2)$, and the criterion (2.18) is unchanged.

As $m_h\to0$ at fixed $L$, for (G2): linear grip $\rho=0$ at every $m_h$ with divergent cost; the branch $\mu F_2<0$ loses its lowest eigenvector; for $\mu_iF_2^{(i)}>0$ the cost is finite, $C^{(1)}=-C^{\rm mark}+O(1)\to\infty$, $\rho_{\rm mark}=1+O(N_fm_h)$, $\rho_{\rm bond}\to0$ for a common grip and $\lvert\rho_{{\rm bond},i}\rvert\to\infty$ for different grips in general.

open_issues: Level-dependent relative corrections O(β²) to (2.17)–(2.18) for (G) are bounded but computed only for (G2), through ζ and u.
The first nonzero mark weights of (2.23) (orders θ³, β⁵), and hence ρ_mark for (Gθ) with T_f = 0, are not computed (not asked by note (c)).
The limit m_h → 0 at fixed L is determined only for (G2) grips.
Fields of 06-ilang-source and 07-ilang-weight, m_h = 0 with an anchor, and the formation speed are outside this package.
Whether the square grip with a common β̂, or the tuned grip 4F₂⟨F⟩₀ = F₁² + ζ, is selected by anything in the language is not addressed (item 6, M10).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of costs, weights, ratios and the small parameters ε², u
The (G) formulas at order μ² reduce to the order-μ² terms of the exact (G2) formulas, including the two-grip bond weight, and the linear grip gives ρ = 0 in both
Square grip at tree level: the shifted cost μF(c)/D_μ is proportional to F(c), consistent with (2.15) at w₀ = ζ = 0
